es.summary: La gliclazida es una sulfonilurea que estimula la liberación de insulina de las células β pancreáticas.
key_points: Aumenta la secreción de insulina dependiente de glucosa.
Usada en DM2 cuando la dieta y metformina no son suficientes.
Principal efecto adverso: hipoglucemia, especialmente en ayuno o ejercicio.
Se metaboliza en el hígado; precaución en insuficiencia hepática.
Contraindicada en embarazo, lactancia y pacientes con hipersensibilidad.

mechanism: Se une a los canales de potasio ATP‑dependientes en células β.
Cierra el canal, despolariza la membrana y abre canales de calcio.
El aumento de Ca²⁺ intracelular promueve la exocitosis de insulina.
indications: Cuando la metformina y cambios de estilo de vida no logran control glucémico.
Adjunto a dieta y ejercicio regular.
adverse_effects: Hipoglucemia (común, grave si no se trata).
interactions: Aumenta riesgo de hipoglucemia con otros antidiabéticos (metformina, insulina).
Potencia hipoglucemia con beta‑bloqueadores y alcohol.
Inhibidores de CYP2C9 (p. ej., fluconazol) pueden elevar niveles.
nursing_care: Verificar glucemia capilar antes de administrar; retener si <70 mg/dL.
Evaluar ingesta de alimentos y actividad física reciente.
Monitorear signos de hipoglucemia: sudoración, temblor, confusión.
Retener dosis y notificar al médico si glucemia <50 mg/dL o síntomas severos.
Registrar hora de administración y respuesta glucémica.
patient_teaching: Tomar el medicamento con alimentos para disminuir riesgo de hipoglucemia.
Reconocer y tratar rápidamente síntomas de hipoglucemia (azúcar, jugo).
No omitir comidas; planificar actividad física y ajustar dosis si es necesario.
Mantener registro de glucemia y reportar valores fuera de rango.
Informar al profesional de salud sobre cualquier nuevo medicamento o suplemento.
antidote_overdose: Glucagón 1 mg IM/IV cada 5‑15 min hasta reversión de hipoglucemia.
Administrar dextrosa 50 % IV si glucosa <40 mg/dL y glucagón contraindicado.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de nivel de glucemia inestable
outcomes: Control de glucemia: mantener glucemia entre 80‑130 mg/dL en ayuno.
Seguridad del paciente: ausencia de episodios hipoglucémicos durante la hospitalización.

interventions.action: Obtener glucemia capilar antes de cada dosis y registrar resultados.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar hipoglucemia y decidir retener o ajustar la dosis.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de hipoglucemia y uso de glucagón de emergencia.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la respuesta rápida y previene complicaciones graves.

interventions.action: Coordinar horarios de comidas y actividad física con la administración del fármaco.
interventions.rationale: Reduce la variabilidad glucémica y el riesgo de hipoglucemia.

interventions.action: Revisar lista de medicamentos para identificar interacciones que potencien hipoglucemia.
interventions.rationale: Previene efectos aditivos que pueden causar niveles peligrosamente bajos de glucosa.

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si se presentan glucemias <70 mg/dL o síntomas de hipoglucemia.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajuste de dosis o cambio de terapia para mantener estabilidad glucémica.

en.summary: Gliclazide is a sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin release from pancreatic β cells.
key_points: Used in type 2 diabetes when diet and metformin are insufficient.
Primary adverse effect: hypoglycemia, especially during fasting or exercise.
Metabolized in the liver; caution in hepatic insufficiency.
Contraindicated in pregnancy, lactation, and patients with hypersensitivity.

mechanism: Binds to ATP‑dependent potassium channels in β cells.
Closes the channel, depolarizes the membrane, and opens calcium channels.
The rise in intracellular Ca²⁺ promotes insulin exocytosis.
indications: When metformin and lifestyle changes fail to achieve glycemic control.
Adjunct to regular diet and exercise.
interactions: Increases risk of hypoglycemia with other antidiabetics (metformin, insulin).
Potentiates hypoglycemia with beta‑blockers and alcohol.
CYP2C9 inhibitors (e.g., fluconazole) can raise levels.
nursing_care: Check capillary glucose before administration; hold if <70 mg/dL (mg/dL).
Assess recent food intake and physical activity.
Monitor for hypoglycemia signs: sweating, tremor, confusion.
Hold dose and notify provider if glucose <50 mg/dL or severe symptoms.
patient_teaching: Take medication with food to reduce hypoglycemia risk.
Recognize and treat hypoglycemia promptly (sugar, juice).
Do not skip meals; plan exercise and adjust dose if needed.
Keep a glucose log and report out‑of‑range values.
antidote_overdose: Glucagon 1 mg IM/IV every 5‑15 min until hypoglycemia reverses.
Administer 50 % dextrose IV if glucose <40 mg/dL and glucagon contraindicated.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for unstable blood glucose level
outcomes: Glucose control: maintain fasting glucose 80‑130 mg/dL.
Patient safety: no hypoglycemic episodes during hospitalization.

interventions.action: Obtain capillary glucose before each dose and record results.
interventions.rationale: Identifies hypoglycemia and guides dose adjustment.

interventions.action: Educate patient on hypoglycemia signs and use of emergency glucagon.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates rapid response and prevents severe complications.

interventions.action: Coordinate meal and activity schedules with medication timing.
interventions.rationale: Reduces glucose variability and hypoglycemia risk.

interventions.action: Review medication list for interactions that potentiate hypoglycemia.
interventions.rationale: Prevents additive effects that could lower glucose dangerously.

interventions.action: Notify provider if glucose <70 mg/dL or hypoglycemia symptoms occur.
interventions.rationale: Allows dose adjustment or therapy change to maintain stability.

sources.name: Pharmacology for Nurses: Insulin and Non-Insulin Injectable Diabetes Drugs

key_points.0.quote: Increases insulin secretion when glucose levels are elevated, decreases glucagon secretion, and delays gastric emptying in an effort to lower postprandial glucose levels

key_points.3.quote: Caution should be used in clients with gastroparesis as amylin analogs may further slow down gastric emptying, in clients with severe renal impairment as the drugs are excreted in the urine and can further impair renal function, and in clients with hepatic insufficiency due to the drugs being metabolized by the liver and thus can impede liver functioning.

sections.indications.2.quote: Indications As an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in individuals older than 10 years of age

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Typical adverse effects of all types of insulin include hypoglycemia (symptoms include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, confusion, and, in severe cases, loss of consciousness), weight gain (due to an increased glucose uptake and storage in cells), injection site reactions (such as redness, swelling, or itching), lipodystrophy (fat tissue changes from repeated use of the same injection site), and fluid retention (swelling in the legs and feet).

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: Adverse effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal discomfort, and loss of appetite.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Orange juice, graham crackers, and hard candy are appropriate carbohydrate choices during hypoglycemia.
